cells.tense: The joy is here now, and you are the one lifting it with both hands.
cells.ask: Pick the thing people should be glad of together, and pour one unhurried hour into it this week — and keep going past the part where the fun turns into duty.
cells.core:
Something in you knows which moments are worth gathering people for, and doesn't put it off until the calendar is clear. The good thing arrives and you're already bringing it to whoever's around, turning what you've been through into something they can take part in. That's why people come when you call them.
You're trusting what has been growing — how it's coming along, who's getting steadier — instead of managing it into shape. That trust is what gives the sharing anything to stand on. So keep the body of it: whatever you raise out loud is only as good as what you've actually been growing. Pick one thing, give it the hour, and let the fun be the part that carries it when it stops being new.
cells.sheetLine: You raise what's worth sharing, and you grow it yourself.

cells.tense: You are counting on something you haven't raised yet, and living inside it ahead of time.
cells.ask: Choose one thing already growing near you, and tend it without checking the results for two weeks.
cells.core:
You can already see the day it comes together — the good room, the meaning finally obvious — and you're living there instead of here. So the person in front of you gets scheduled, and the thing they're actually working through gets skipped. Standing that close to the future makes now look like equipment.
The tell is that you've begun arranging people for the version of them that's coming, skipping how they're doing today. Nothing grows under that. You know how to make something last; you've done it before. Bring it here — pick one person or one piece already coming along and give it two ordinary weeks with nothing owed at the end. Let it surprise you slowly.

cells.tense: The sharing went quiet, and some part of you is still standing at a door that's closed behind you.
cells.ask: Go deeper into one subject you actually love, and tell someone what you came out believing.
cells.core:
The sharing went quiet, and the care went private. You tend one thing at a time — proof it's working — but nothing gets handed around where others can take part. Things still get grown here. The telling over stopped.
There's a corner of your mind you've kept exploring on your own, and that's the way back in — go further into it than usual, past where you can already see the end, and find one thing worth believing out loud. When it's real to you, it goes to somebody: the person who'd actually want to hear it. Deep, then said. Not crowd-sized. One person is enough.

cells.tense: The care is already running in the room, and you are calling it just being practical.
cells.ask: Say out loud, to one person, what you noticed growing in them — and let that be the whole point of the sentence.
cells.core:
You notice where people are in their own progress and say the thing that opens them up — the right word at the right time, no ceremony around it. Ask the people who work beside you; they feel the difference, and it shapes how they keep going. That's what this looks like when it's working: naming what's growing in someone so it lands, and the naming is what carries it forward.
But you file it under housekeeping, and it doesn't get counted as something you did. What you see plainly might mean something because you said it, not despite you. Choose one person, one thing you've watched them get better at, and say it out loud without anything attached — no advice, no next step, done when the sentence is. You'll recognize the feeling. It's yours, and you can start taking it.
cells.sheetLine: You're part of why this gets noticed. It can be called yours.
